instruction:
You are a senior civil engineer specializing in water infrastructure and pipe hydraulics.

## Problem

Calculate the friction head loss in a pressurised pipe using the Hazen-Williams equation. Determine the hydraulic gradient and mean flow velocity.

## Given

| Parameter | Value | Unit |
|-----------|-------|------|
| Flow rate (Q) | {{ flow_rate_l_s }} | L/s |
| Pipe diameter (D) | {{ pipe_diameter_mm }} | mm |
| Pipe length (L) | {{ pipe_length_m }} | m |
{% if c_factor is defined %}
| Hazen-Williams C-factor | {{ c_factor }} | — |
{% endif %}
{% if archetype_description is defined %}

### Pipe Conditions

{{ archetype_description }}
{% endif %}

{% if tool_available %}
## Available Tool

A head loss calculation tool is available at `/workspace/hazen-williams-headloss_calc.py`. Run it with:

```bash
python3 /workspace/hazen-williams-headloss_calc.py --help
```

You may use this tool to verify your calculations or compute values directly.
{% endif %}

## Required

Calculate the following:

1. Friction head loss hf (m)
2. Hydraulic gradient S (dimensionless)
3. Mean flow velocity V (m/s)

## Applicable Standards

- AWWA — American Water Works Association pipe flow references
- AS/NZS 3500 — Australian/New Zealand plumbing and drainage standard

## Constraints

- No internet access is available. Work from engineering knowledge and the provided tool.
- Use the following formulas:
  - Convert flow rate: Q (m³/s) = Q (L/s) / 1000
  - Convert diameter: D (m) = D (mm) / 1000
  - Hazen-Williams head loss (SI): hf = 10.67 × L × Q¹·⁸⁵² / (C¹·⁸⁵² × D⁴·⁸⁷)
    where Q is in m³/s, D is in metres, L is in metres
  - Hydraulic gradient: S = hf / L
  - Flow velocity: V = Q / (π × D² / 4) where Q and D are in SI units
- If the Hazen-Williams C-factor is not given, you must infer an appropriate value from the pipe material description.

## Output Format

Show your step-by-step working in Markdown, including the unit conversions, head loss calculation, hydraulic gradient, and velocity. At the end of your solution, include a JSON block with your final answers in exactly this format:

```json
{
  "head_loss_m": <numeric_value>,
  "hydraulic_gradient": <numeric_value>,
  "flow_velocity_m_s": <numeric_value>
}
```

Write your complete solution to `/workspace/output.md`.
paramsToml:
[meta]
name = "hazen-williams-headloss"
description = "Friction head loss calculation using the Hazen-Williams empirical equation"
long_description = "Calculates friction head loss in pressurised water mains using the Hazen-Williams empirical formula hf = 10.67 * L * Q^1.852 / (C^1.852 * D^4.87), along with the hydraulic gradient and flow velocity. The C-factor encodes pipe material and condition. Widely used in municipal water distribution design per AWWA and AS/NZS 3500 for sizing pipes and evaluating network pressure losses."
discipline = "civil"
category = "pipe-hydraulics"
standards = ["AWWA", "AS/NZS 3500"]
tags = ["civil", "pipe-hydraulics", "head-loss", "hazen-williams", "deterministic"]
tool_mode = "with-tool"

[params.flow_rate_l_s]
type = "float"
unit = "L/s"
description = "Volumetric flow rate Q"
min = 0.5
max = 500.0

[params.pipe_diameter_mm]
type = "float"
unit = "mm"
description = "Internal pipe diameter D"
min = 50
max = 2000

[params.pipe_length_m]
type = "float"
unit = "m"
description = "Pipe length L"
min = 10
max = 5000

[params.c_factor]
type = "float"
description = "Hazen-Williams roughness coefficient C"
min = 60
max = 150
derivable_from = "archetype"

# --- Outputs ---

[outputs.head_loss_m]
description = "Friction head loss hf (m)"
tolerance = 0.03

[outputs.hydraulic_gradient]
description = "Hydraulic gradient S = hf / L (dimensionless)"
tolerance = 0.05

[outputs.flow_velocity_m_s]
description = "Mean flow velocity V (m/s)"
tolerance = 0.03

# --- Archetypes ---
# Pipe material scenarios that determine the Hazen-Williams C-factor.

[archetypes.new_pvc]
description = "New PVC or HDPE pipeline"
c_factor = {min = 140, max = 150}
site_contexts = ["sydney-greenfield", "brisbane-suburban"]

[archetypes.new_ductile_iron]
description = "New cement-lined ductile iron pipeline"
c_factor = {min = 130, max = 140}
site_contexts = ["melbourne-trunk-main", "adelaide-distribution"]

[archetypes.aged_cast_iron]
description = "Aged unlined cast iron pipeline with moderate tuberculation"
c_factor = {min = 80, max = 100}
site_contexts = ["sydney-inner-west-legacy", "melbourne-inner-legacy"]

[archetypes.corroded_steel]
description = "Corroded steel water main"
c_factor = {min = 60, max = 80}
site_contexts = ["darwin-industrial-reticulation", "cairns-coastal-reticulation"]

# --- Difficulty ---

[difficulty.easy]
description = "All parameters given, smooth new pipe, moderate flow"
visibility = "all_given"
archetypes = ["new_pvc", "new_ductile_iron"]

[difficulty.medium]
description = "All parameters given, any pipe material and flow regime"
visibility = "all_given"
archetypes = ["new_pvc", "new_ductile_iron", "aged_cast_iron", "corroded_steel"]

[difficulty.hard]
description = "C-factor hidden, agent must infer from pipe material description"
visibility = "partial"
hidden_params = ["c_factor"]
replacement_text = "The pipe is a {{ archetype.description }} ({{ archetype.site_context }})"
archetypes = ["new_pvc", "new_ductile_iron", "aged_cast_iron", "corroded_steel"]
